To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the trunk muscle activity was significantly higher during the 80 kg squat and deadlift exercises compared with the body weight squat and deadlift as well as compared with the superman and sidebridge exercises.
the trunk muscles of the erector spinae were activated significantly more during 80% of the 1 repetition maximum squat and deadlift compared to other exercises.

trunk muscle activation during upright, resisted, and dynamic exercises can achieve levels of muscle activity that exceed those of the same exercises with the same resistance performed with body weight or with instability devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new, non-invasive, and reliable method for measuring the thickness of the subcutaneous fat layer of the trunk.
trunk muscle activation during dynamic, resisted, weight-training and isometrics exercises.
the development of the trunk musculature in relation to the performance of dynamic exercises.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trunk muscle activation is greater during dynamic resistance exercises than isometric instability activities.
the trunk muscle activation during dynamic resistance training exercises is sufficient to elicit a training effect.
the 80%1 RM squat significantly exceeded the body weight, 80% 80% 100% 1RM, and 100% 80%1RM deadlift squat exercises by 34.6, 56.7, 56.8, and 53%, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dynamic, resisted, upright exercises can provide high levels of core activation, which is not always the case with isometric, unstable exercise.
the addition of unstable devices may be unnecessary when performing upright, resisted dynamic exercises.
the trunk musculature can be effectively trained with dynamic resistance exercises and that the addition of instability exercises may be unnecessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that

individuals performing upright, resisted dynamic exercises such as squats and dead-lifts can achieve high levels of trunk muscle activation and therefore do not need to add unstable devices to augment core stability exercises.
individuals who are training for strength and power can get the same benefits from traditional strength training as those who are performing exercises that are more focused on core stability.
dynamic, upright, resistance training exercises can provide significant activation to the trunk musculature.
